title: Big: Your Wish Is Granted
description: A carnival wish, a giant piano, and one very strange party—five steps into Tom Hanks' Big.
imageHint: Large piano keyboard on the floor of a toy store with someone dancing on the keys

questions.question: Too short for a carnival ride, kid Josh Baskin feeds a quarter to what fortune-teller machine and wishes to be big?
questions.explanation: The prop was modeled on a real late-'60s arcade machine called Zoltan. Zoltar Speaks got so famous that a company trademarked the name in 2007 and started selling real ones.

questions.question: Wish granted by Zoltar, grown-up Josh meets his boss at FAO Schwarz. They stomp out "Chopsticks" on the giant floor piano, plus what other duet?
questions.explanation: Hanks and Robert Loggia practiced on cardboard keyboards at home, and the studio hired doubles just in case. They didn't need them. Penny Marshall added "Chopsticks."

questions.question: The Heart and Soul duet wins Josh a promotion and an invite to a fancy party, where he eats what tiny appetizer row by row, typewriter-style?
questions.explanation: Penny Marshall: "I picked up a piece of corn and just signaled, and he went, 'Yeah, got it.'" The caviar he spits out was in the script; the corn was pure improv.

questions.question: Baby corn aside, Josh's real gift is toys. When a rival pitches a robot that turns into a building, Josh asks what's fun about that. What's his own big idea?
questions.explanation: It's a choose-your-own-adventure story on a handheld screen, basically the text adventure Josh plays at home. Fans later built a real version of that game.

questions.question: Long before his comic book pitch, Josh noticed something impossible about Zoltar the night he made his wish. What was it?
questions.explanation: The card says "Your wish is granted." Then Josh looks down and sees the plug lying on the ground. Nobody in the movie ever explains it, and nobody needs to.

easterEgg.title: The other Josh
easterEgg.text: Robert De Niro was actually cast as grown-up Josh until the deal fell apart. Elizabeth Perkins on his version: "a little more of a horror movie. Robert De Niro wandering around the streets of New York."
